title: Grain
objective: Add Lightroom-familiar synthetic film grain (Amount, Size, Roughness) as a finish-stage module with an exact reference, a GPU program, generated controls and API, preset import, rendered evidence and measurements, then align its responses with Lightroom's.
context_summary: Grain is a positional colour unit after the vignette: a pure function of the full-resolution output pixel, three strengths and a frozen seed, so it needs no host stage, halo or cache. Decided: Size in full-resolution output pixels (G1). Recorded defaults: its own section after Vignette, a fixed seed, luminance grain, order after the vignette, statistically matched reduced-stage frames reported not gated. The study's numerics are delegated within the design's contract. The owner authorized implementation. The study, the module, the GPU program, the preset mapping, the desktop section with its smoke scenario and the rig are delivered and verified on Linux (the GPU on RADV, the smoke under Xvfb); the M4 qualification and measurement remain, and the owner's Lightroom export is needed only by the final alignment task. Minimum model: the high tier; re-review against current main before each task.

tasks.description: Freeze grain's numerics in a study: the hash, the noise field, the Size and Roughness mappings, the tone weight, the application, the reduced-stage rule and the tolerances, with an independent f64 reference and fixtures.
extra_context: Done: grain-study.md, crates/luxforge-reference/src/grain.rs and fixtures/grain/ with its README freeze the hash, field, mappings, tone weight, application, reduced-stage rule and tolerances.

Deliver docs/design/grain-study.md, crates/luxforge-reference/src/grain.rs and fixtures/grain/ (with a README), in the vignette study's shape: frozen equations in the exact form and order a production unit transcribes, worked examples, property proofs, the frozen tolerance and limitations. No module, GPU program or UI here.

Requirements are the design's processing contract: grain at an output pixel is a function only of its integer full-resolution output position, the three strengths and one frozen seed constant; lattice values come from a u32 wrapping integer hash that WGSL computes identically; the field has zero mean, unit standard deviation and bounded tails for every Size and Roughness; Size is in full-resolution output pixels (decided G1), Size 0 about one pixel; Roughness changes irregularity at fixed strength; luminance only, in the tone study's encoded domain with luminance-ratio reconstruction and the near-black rule; a tone weight vanishing at black and white; mean-preserving on flat fields; values above white unchanged; Amount 0 the exact identity.

The reduced-stage rule: at a stage reduced by s per side (CompileStage::scale), evaluate the field at each stage pixel's centre in full-resolution coordinates, band-limited and attenuated so its standard deviation per tone and its radially averaged spectrum match the full-resolution grain reduced by the same linear-light area average, within a frozen statistical tolerance, measured at s of 2, 4 and 8.

Delegated to the implementer within that contract: the noise construction (lattice gradient or value noise, octave count, a clumping modulation), the Size and Roughness mappings to the field's scale and irregularity, the tone weight's shape, the amplitude Amount 100 reaches, and the statistical tolerances. Choose amplitudes so Amount 100 is clearly visible film grain at 100% without clipping a mid-grey's grain; Lightroom's responses are fitted later, so no Lightroom equivalence is claimed.

The reference uses luxforge-reference's own sRGB and tone helpers and never depends on luxforge-core. Fixtures are hand-built: flat fields at several tones, a grey wedge, saturated colours, black, white, RAW headroom above white, each slider at its ends, and reduced-stage pairs.

acceptance_criteria: grain-study.md freezes every equation and constant, the reduced-stage rule and the tolerances, and lists its limitations; the fixtures README names each fixture and its expected values.

Reference tests prove on the fixtures: Amount 0 identity; zero mean and unit standard deviation of the field within the study's bound for Size and Roughness at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100; mean preservation per tone; black, white and above-white invariance; chroma preserved by the luminance-ratio reconstruction; the field's dependence on position alone (the same value from any tile or window origin); the reduced-stage statistics within the frozen tolerance at s of 2, 4 and 8.
The hash is written in u32 wrapping operations only, with a test vector table a WGSL transcription can be checked against.

tasks.description: Implement the luxforge.grain module: a finish-stage field-patch layer at order 10 with Amount, Size and Roughness, its positional colour unit transcribed from the study, edit.set-grain and edit.reset-grain, presets and copy groups, and the conformance suite.
extra_context: Done: luxforge.grain (luxforge.grain.film, payload format 1, finish order 10) with edit.set-grain and edit.reset-grain, the conformance suite, the editor-acceptance placement chapter, the Grain preset and copy group and the usage tool registry entry.

Follow the vignette module: crates/luxforge-core/src/modules/grain/{mod.rs,unit.rs}, effect luxforge.grain.film at payload format 1 listed in BUILTIN_FORMATS, EffectStage::Finish with declared order 10 so a grain layer always follows the vignette, single_layer, a missing key meaning the field's default (Amount 0, Size 25, Roughness 50), neutral exactly when Amount is 0, collapsed, one group, presettable, not maskable. Registry position after Vignette.

The unit is one PointwiseColor that reads the row's y and starting x, maps stage pixels to full-resolution output pixels through CompileStage::scale and full, and transcribes the study's equations in the same form and order as grain.rs, so the full-resolution path is within the study's exact tolerance; a reduced stage uses the study's reduced-stage rule. It allocates no table proportional to the frame. Strengths go through a response.json read by modules/response.rs with identity knots for now, so the later fold changes data, not code.

Add grain to the field-patch conformance suite and to the editor-acceptance chapter that covers finish-layer placement (presence_mixer_vignette_acceptance.rs or a chapter of its own): grain after the vignette whichever is committed first, and a crop update leaving the grain field's scale unchanged.
Without a GPU program the desktop draws a grain stack through the reference renderer with the layer named by the no-program fallback; that is correct until the next task lands the program.
Answer the performance checklist in the handoff and record the reference's per-frame cost of the unit at 24 MP and 60 MP as an indication.

tasks.description: Give grain its GPU program and qualification corpus recipes: the unit in WGSL with the study's hash, device tests against the reference, and grain-* recipes in the preview corpus.
extra_context: Done on Linux RADV: unit.wgsl (lf_grain_film) in GPU_PROGRAMS, the gpu_grain device tests and ten grain-* recipes in the corpus's grain family. Not run there: the RAW cells, which need the private RAW manifest. grain-straightened-crop on derived-paged misses at Fit, 33% and 50% by the one-pixel frame-size mismatch plain crop-straightened has there, which grain does not cause. The M4 whole-corpus gate is the qualification task's.

crates/luxforge-core/src/modules/grain/unit.wgsl as a Colour-kind GpuProgram listed in GPU_PROGRAMS, placed by the plan in output space after the geometry tail as the vignette's is, receiving the full-resolution origin and scale so a window, a tile and a reduced stage address the study's field. The hash's u32 test vectors from the study are checked on the device.

Add grain-* recipes to fixtures/preview/corpus.json: Amount 100 at Size 0, 25 and 100 and Roughness 0 and 100, a default-settings recipe, grain over a dark vignette, grain under a straightened crop, and grain on a RAW stack, each in the pointwise class and in a grain family, so --families grain runs them alone.

Device tests run where an adapter exists (the Linux host's RADV or the M4's Metal). The whole-corpus gate on the M4 belongs to the qualification task; run the grain-* cells here on whatever native adapter is available and report the host.
If a program cannot meet the pointwise limit, that is a defect of the program; do not widen the limit.

tasks.description: Extend the Lightroom alignment rig with grain families measured as statistics: generate Amount, Size and Roughness variants, measure grain strength per tone, feature size and irregularity, and fit maps, with Luxforge's own round fitting as the identity.
extra_context: Done: the rig's grain-amount, grain-size and grain-roughness families, measured as statistics with known-answer tests, and an identity round on Luxforge's own renders; lightroom-alignment.md describes them.

Grain is random, so pixels cannot be compared between the two editors. Measure on flat fields at several greys and on the spatial chart at 2400 x 1600 and 6000 x 4000 (which tests whether Lightroom's grain size follows the picture's size, the decided G1 being output pixels): the standard deviation of L* per tone (strength and tone weight), the radially averaged power spectrum's peak and half-power frequency (size), and a clumping statistic such as the spread of local variance or kurtosis (roughness), with the mean shift reported.

Variants: Amount at 10, 25, 50, 75, 100 with Size 25 and Roughness 50; Size at 0 to 100 and Roughness at 0 to 100 with Amount 50 held. Measures and fits belong in luxforge-reference's lr_align study with synthetic cases of known answer; orchestration in xtask's lr_align. A held field's Amount converts through its own family's map, as the vignette's Midpoint does.

The owner's Lightroom export is not needed here: the rig is proved by a round of Luxforge's own renders, which must fit as the identity. Update the alignment design's measured-settings table and rig sections for grain.

tasks.description: Align grain's responses with Lightroom: the owner's grain round, the fold of Amount, Size and Roughness into the module's responses at payload format 2, requalification, and the owner's review of the sheets.
extra_context: The one external input: the owner imports the grain round into a scratch Lightroom catalog and exports it as the rig's instructions say. Measure it, fold each field's map into response.json (level B), raise the effect's payload format to 2 so a format-1 layer is refused, and rerun the grain-* cells of gpu-qualification on a native adapter.

Report level C candidates by the alignment design's threshold: a tone weight of a different shape, a size that follows the picture's size (Lightroom being frame-relative would not change the decided G1 without the owner), or a roughness no map can match. Prepare the contact sheets for the owner's review of the look.
